proposed_core_edits.reason: The active directive requires the anchor construction to state the convexity of the compact ambient outcome domain explicitly and to record that the broader local families need not be nested in the shell radius.

prose_updates.tldr: For binary outcomes on a growing uniform covariate partition, the sharp absolute-cost COT lower endpoint is \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\), where \(\rho_K\) is the realized correlation of two deterministic sign arrays. When \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\) remains finite and triple collisions vanish, a Poisson number of cross-arm collisions carries the minimax information: parameter-free supported-mixture kernels and a uniform deterministic-array approximation yield exact minimax absolute-risk and honest-length transfer, with shrinking rational interval-action certificates and explicit tail, off-grid coverage, and rounding errors. When \(\lambda_K\) diverges sparsely, the unprojected estimator is uniformly studentized Gaussian and the deterministic-shell local minimax theorem gives the matching interior variance frontier. Embedding cell \(j\) as \(j/K\) transfers the finite frontiers and, through pointwise shell inclusion followed by the ordered lower limits, the local variance as converse lower bounds to every anchor-admissible containing class. No broader-class upper bound is claimed; continuous achievability remains confined to the declared growing-roughness interpolation image.

project_justification.gap: Published COT theory supplies the general sharp conditional-transport endpoint under compact-domain and continuous-cost hypotheses, but it does not characterize the marked-Poisson information experiment created by sparse cross-arm replication on a growing partition. Large-alphabet collision theory and confidence-set duality supply ingredients, not the two-arm realized endpoint, certified interval-action enclosure, uniform deterministic-array transfer, or converse transfer to arbitrary containing anchor classes.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a single collision-indexed information frontier: exact finite-information decisions when \(\lambda_K\) is bounded, Gaussian local efficiency when it diverges sparsely, and a precise account of which lower bounds pass from the finite stress test to broader COT classes even when their local families are not nested in the shell radius.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a marked-Poisson reduction with parameter-free forward and reverse randomization under shell-conditioned legal mixtures, derives uniform collision approximation for every deterministic array, certifies finite-information intervals by exact rational lower-dual and upper-primal witnesses with continuum coverage repair, and establishes the ordered LAN-to-deterministic-shell local minimax theorem. The finite arrays embed into the compact-covariate, compact-convex-outcome Bernoulli-design COT anchor. Subclass monotonicity then transfers both finite-intensity frontiers and, using \(\lim_{T\to\infty}\liminf_{H\to\infty}\liminf_{K\to\infty}\), the local truncated-quadratic variance as converse lower bounds to every containing class. Collision-based upper bounds are not claimed for those broader classes.

prose_updates.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS, Theorems 1--6) establish general sharp COT bounds, continuity, and statistical guarantees. Their Theorem~1 is the identification anchor under a compact covariate domain, compact convex ambient outcome domain, overlap, and a continuous objective; the affine binary endpoint here is a separately proved specialization, and the embedded arrays satisfy that anchor setup. The anchor-containing-class theorem transfers collision lower bounds upward only by submodel monotonicity. It does not claim collision achievability over the broader class, and alternating embedded signs need not satisfy later uniform smoothness or rate hypotheses. Their smooth-density follow-up uses Proposition~3.2 for its main estimation bound, Proposition~3.3 for quadratic-objective stability, and Theorem~3.2 for asymptotic normality; atomic binary outcomes and absolute cost instead lead to marked-collision likelihoods. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.5) provide model-agnostic dual inference and emphasize binning loss, but do not optimize honest expected length or identify this collision frontier. Ober-Reynolds (2023) derives sharp OT intervals and root-\(n\) inference in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model, not sparse covariate collisions. Paninski (2008) and Kipnis (2026) show that collisions govern sparse large-alphabet testing; Kipnis's supported-mixture architecture is especially close, but concerns one-sample uniformity testing. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, Theorem~1) supply dependency-neighborhood Poisson approximation. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem~1 and Corollary~1) and Stoye (2009, Propositions~1--2) inform confidence-set duality and boundary repair, but do not supply the tail truncation, likelihood modulus, endpoint expansion, or exact rational verification here. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem~3) provide a limit-experiment efficiency template; the supported-shell argument here proves the ordered deterministic-array local minimax statement for bounded truncated quadratic losses. Low and Zhou (2007) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2021) motivate the restricted pushforward and bias-aware scope, without supporting an upper claim over a full smoothness ball.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The former two-fixed-array lower witness is invalid because armwise marginal imbalance reveals the endpoint without cross-arm collisions. Every lower bound therefore uses mixtures supported on legal arrays and pays the discrepancy between the mixture index and the realized \(L_K\). Floating-point linear-program output may only propose a basis: a certificate exists only after every likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual quantity is outward-rounded and the rational inequalities are checked exactly. Endpoint decisions may be clipped to \(\mathcal D\) without increasing absolute or squared loss, but projection of \(\widehat L_K\) onto the narrower \(\mathcal A\) is excluded from the local Gaussian theorem because it changes boundary risk. The broader local classes need not be nested in \(H\), so their transfer uses \(\liminf_{H\to\infty}\), not an asserted limit.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The finite-\(\lambda\) comparison and decision theorems concern the realized endpoint \(L_K\) over the full legal deterministic-array class. Rational interval certificates require computable inputs and exact outward-rounded likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual checks; floating-point output alone is not a certificate. The sparse theorem gives unprojected studentized Gaussian inference and the matching ordered deterministic-shell local minimax variance at interior correlations. Embedded finite-array laws meet the compact-covariate, compact-convex-outcome, continuous-cost COT identification anchor, so their global minimax frontiers transfer by lower limits to every containing class. For arbitrary nonnested local containing families, only the ordered converse \(\lim_{T\to\infty}\liminf_{H\to\infty}\liminf_{K\to\infty}\) is claimed. There is no broader-class collision upper bound or equality. Continuous achievability transfers only through the declared interpolation-image kernels; no raw total-variation comparison is asserted between continuous covariates and discrete labels. No claim covers unknown amplitudes, nonuniform cells, nonnegligible triple collisions, or a full continuous smoothness class. Coarsening changes the endpoint unless a separate bias theorem is supplied.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem places the collision frontiers inside the broader COT anchor without extending the collision procedures beyond the embedded arrays.
statement_notes.gap: The anchor identification theorem supplies the sharp conditional-transport target, but not finite-collision or local-minimax lower bounds for every class containing the deterministic-array submodel.
statement_notes.consumer: Researchers can use the collision frontier as a certified impossibility benchmark for any anchor-admissible method, while keeping broader-class achievability separate.
